items.title: 4.1.7.2 Types of Trees (Binary Tree, AVL Trees)

source_refs.note: Topic 4.1.7.2 Types of Trees (PDF 111-112, printed 108-109). Figure 4.10 draws 30 on the left and 15 on the right, mirrored relative to the text; the original diagram follows the text. Recorded.

items: Binary tree: each node has at most two children, the left and right child. In a family example, Grandparent is the root with children Parent1 and Parent2, and each parent can have its own children such as Child1 and Child2 (Figure 4.9).

AVL tree: a binary tree that keeps itself balanced. If one side grows too tall compared with the other, the tree rearranges itself. In the example rooted at 20, the left side holds 15, 10 and 18 and the right side 30, and the height difference stays minimal (Figure 4.10).

blocks.alt: Binary tree of circles joined by arrows: Grandparent at the top points to Parent2 and Parent1; Parent2 points to Child4 and Child3; Parent1 points to Child2 and Child1.
blocks.caption: Figure 4.9: Binary Tree Representation of a Family Tree (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 4.9).

blocks.alt: AVL tree with arrows: 20 at the top; 15 as its left child, with 10 on the left and 18 on the right under it; 30 as the right child of 20.
blocks.caption: Figure 4.10: AVL Tree (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 4.10, with 15, 10 and 18 on the left and 30 on the right as the text describes).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 4.10 is mirrored, with 30 on the left and 15 on the right (18 left of 15); as the text says, 15 (with 10 on its left and 18 on its right) is on the left of 20 and 30 on the right, as drawn above.
